newsitem.title: CHINA: China says France wise on human rights motion.
newsitem.headline: China says France wise on human rights motion.

text.p: China on Monday applauded France's decision not to co-sponsor a U.N. motion critical of Beijing's human rights record, saying Paris had chosen cooperation over confrontation.

France said last week it would not co-sponsor a motion to criticise China's rights policies at the United Nations Human Rights Convention in Geneva, citing what it said was progress by Beijing on protecting fundamental freedoms.
"This is a wise decision and an action worthy of approval," the Overseas Edition of China's official People's Daily said in an editorial.
Paris had turned away from the road of confrontation and any criticism of the French move was unfounded, the newspaper said.
"Some people have used this to attack France, but that is entirely unreasonable and just reflects their anxiety in the face of the defeat of their actions against China," it said.

The United States has said it plans to go ahead with the resolution, which has been put forward with the European Union every year since China crushed pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 1989.
China has so far escaped official censure by mustering support from developing nations, and the European Union is divided on whether to support the motion this year.
Despite France's decision not to push the resolution, China's tribulations in Geneva were not yet over, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said.
It warned those seeking to use human rights as an excuse to engage in anti-China policies, saying only constructive dialogue could help to create a consensus on rights.
"Using human rights to oppose China can only hurt the feelings of the Chinese people and harm relations between China and the relevant countries," it said.

"We would advise certain people to understand the times, rethink their relevant positions, and not to walk further down the evil road of confrontation until they become an obstacle to progress on human rights," it said.
